rules.name: AML — Customer Due Diligence and Ongoing Transaction Monitoring
rules.source_legislation: Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (MLR 2017) as amended; Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (POCA); Terrorism Act 2000
rules.description: The bank must apply Customer Due Diligence (CDD) to all customers at onboarding and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) to higher-risk customers (PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, complex ownership structures). Ongoing transaction monitoring must be applied to all accounts to detect suspicious activity. Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) must be submitted to the National Crime Agency (NCA) within 5 business days of forming a suspicion. The Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) holds senior manager accountability under SM&CR.
approval_chain: Board Risk Committee (for annual MLRO report)
disclosure_obligations: Annual MLRO report to the Board covering SAR volumes, typologies, system performance, and resourcing
SAR submission to NCA within 5 business days of forming a suspicion (tipping-off prohibition applies)
Cooperation with NCA, FCA, and HMRC requests for information under MLR 2017 and POCA
Annual MLR compliance report to supervisory authority (FCA or HMRC depending on business line)
constraints: CDD must be completed before a business relationship is established or a one-off transaction above €15,000 is executed
EDD required for all PEPs, customers from high-risk third countries, correspondent banking relationships, and complex structures
The bank must not tip off a customer that a SAR has been or may be submitted
Transaction monitoring systems must provide demonstrable coverage of 100% of customer accounts — not a statistical sample

rules.name: OFSI Financial Sanctions — Real-Time Screening Obligation
rules.source_legislation: UK Financial Sanctions (OFSI regulations under Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018); Policing and Crime Act 2017 (OFSI civil penalties)
rules.description: The bank must screen all customers, counterparties, and transactions against OFSI's Consolidated List of financial sanctions targets in real time, including screening through corporate ownership chains to identify indirect sanctions exposure. There is no safe harbour for name-matching failures in beneficial ownership chains. OFSI enforcement is increasing — Standard Chartered received a £7.5m civil penalty in 2024 for sanctions violations. The bank must conduct quarterly reviews of its screening system's coverage and accuracy.
disclosure_obligations: Report to OFSI within 14 days of discovering that a customer is a designated person or holds frozen assets
Annual sanctions compliance programme overview to the Board
Maintain records of all screening hits (including cleared hits) for minimum 5 years
constraints: Screening must occur in real time before transactions are processed — batch-end screening is not compliant
Beneficial ownership chain screening required — not name-only matching at the immediate counterparty level
Any match against OFSI Consolidated List must be escalated immediately and the transaction blocked pending MLRO review
OFSI-designated persons' assets must be frozen — no transaction processing or account access permitted without OFSI licence

rules.name: Failure to Prevent Fraud — Corporate Criminal Liability
rules.source_legislation: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 — Failure to Prevent Fraud offence; commencement order expected 2025
rules.description: The bank as a large organisation (turnover >£36m, balance sheet >£18m, or >250 employees) will face corporate criminal liability if an associated person (employee, agent, or subsidiary) commits fraud for the bank's benefit and the bank cannot demonstrate it had reasonable fraud prevention procedures in place. This creates a strict-liability corporate criminal offence unless the bank has a documented and implemented fraud prevention framework. The MLRO and compliance function must ensure the framework is designed, communicated, and tested.
disclosure_obligations: Fraud prevention procedures documented and communicated to all relevant staff and associated persons
Annual board attestation that reasonable fraud prevention procedures are in place
Staff training completion records maintained for inspection by the regulator or court
constraints: The only defence to a failure-to-prevent fraud charge is proof of adequate fraud prevention procedures — the burden is on the bank
Fraud prevention procedures must cover both external fraud and internal fraud committed by employees for the bank's benefit
Procedures must be reviewed annually and updated when material changes to business model or fraud typologies occur

rules.name: SM&CR — Senior Manager Conduct Rules and Prescribed Responsibilities
rules.source_legislation: Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (as amended by the Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013 and Financial Services and Markets Act 2023); FCA/PRA SM&CR Rules; FCA SYSC 4, 5, 6
rules.description: All Senior Manager Function (SMF) holders must be pre-approved by the FCA and/or PRA before taking up their role. They must have statements of responsibilities identifying their prescribed responsibilities. All staff in certified functions must be certified as fit and proper annually. Individual conduct rules apply to all relevant persons. Breach of a conduct rule by an SMF holder may result in FCA/PRA prohibition, financial penalty, or criminal prosecution. The bank must maintain a complete and current SMF register.
disclosure_obligations: SMF applications submitted to FCA/PRA before appointment — pre-approval required
Statement of Responsibilities (SoR) for each SMF holder filed with FCA/PRA and updated on change
Annual certification of all Certified Function holders signed off by the Compliance function
Regulatory references provided and obtained for new SMF/Certified Function hires — mandatory
constraints: No individual may perform an SMF without FCA/PRA pre-approval
Temporary cover for SMF roles permitted for up to 12 weeks without FCA/PRA approval; must be notified
Conduct rules apply to all bank employees — not just SMF holders and Certified Functions
A handover certificate is required when an SMF holder leaves — ensuring continuity of accountability

rules.name: FCA Digital Regulatory Reporting — Machine-Readable Data Delivery
rules.source_legislation: FCA Digital Regulatory Reporting (DRR) pilot; FCA Data Strategy 2022–2025; PRA CP4/24 (modernising regulatory returns)
rules.description: The FCA has signalled ambition for machine-readable, near-real-time regulatory data submission, moving away from batch XBRL filings toward API-based data delivery. The bank must participate in the FCA's DRR pilot programme and prepare its reporting infrastructure for the transition. PRA CP4/24 will rationalise some existing returns and introduce new data standards. Banks dependent on manual return preparation face increasing operational and compliance risk as the regulator raises data quality expectations.
disclosure_obligations: Regulatory returns submitted on time and in the mandated format — XBRL/COREP/FINREP as currently required
DRR pilot participation reported to the Board with timeline and resource estimate
Material reporting failures or late submissions reported to the Audit Committee
constraints: All COREP and FINREP returns must be submitted within PRA/FCA prescribed deadlines — no grace period without supervisory agreement
Data quality remediation plans must be in place for any identified systematic errors in regulatory returns
Banks must be capable of responding to ad-hoc PRA/FCA data requests within the stipulated response window

rules.name: Perpetual KYC — Event-Driven Client Review Expectation
rules.source_legislation: MLR 2017 (as expected to be amended); JMLSG Guidance updates (anticipated 2025–2026); FCA AML supervisory expectations
rules.description: FCA and JMLSG guidance is expected to move from requiring periodic KYC refresh cycles (typically 1, 3, or 5 years by risk tier) to event-driven, risk-based review (perpetual KYC or pKYC). Banks must trigger CDD/EDD reviews based on material changes in customer risk indicators (change of beneficial ownership, adverse media hit, jurisdiction change, unusual transaction pattern) rather than calendar schedules alone. Banks without pKYC infrastructure will face supervisory criticism and potential enforcement.
disclosure_obligations: Annual MLRO report to include pKYC coverage rate and number of event-triggered reviews conducted
FCA supervisory questionnaire responses on KYC refresh methodology and system capabilities
Audit trail of pKYC triggers and review outcomes maintained for minimum 5 years
constraints: Periodic review cycles cannot be the sole trigger for KYC refresh — risk-event triggers must also be automated
Adverse media monitoring must run continuously on all higher-risk and corporate customers
pKYC system must maintain an auditable log of every trigger event and the resultant action taken
